Documentation / Developer / User Manual Pipeline

User Manual Pipeline

Source ownership and consumers

docs/user/*.md is the canonical English user manual. Its human-readable navigation and inventory are owned by the user index; do not maintain a second page list. Keep these English paths stable for repository and website links, without moving them under en/ or duplicating them under locales/en/.

The same Markdown source is intended for GitHub repository browsing, perastage.luismaperamato.com, and packaged offline Perastage help. Consumers must not maintain independent user-workflow prose. Generated web and package outputs are artifacts; permanent edits belong in the canonical Markdown. Developer and reference documentation remains English-only unless explicitly decided otherwise.

Static website consumer

Run node tools/docs/build_static_docs.cjs independently of the application build. It uses vendored Marked 4.3.0 at generation time and derives each channel's grouped navigation from its own docs/user/index.md. Next is generated from the current working tree into docs/next/; Stable is a frozen snapshot from the latest published non-prerelease release tag under docs/stable/. Developer Markdown follows main at adjacent docs/developer/*.html routes; it is never duplicated into user channels. English HTML is committed under docs/; verify it with node tools/docs/build_static_docs.cjs --check. Generated HTML must never receive manual editorial fixes. Edit Markdown and regenerate instead. Packaged Help and the website are separate consumers of the same canonical source; the website does not fetch or render Markdown in the browser. Legacy doc.html?md= bookmarks and root build/repository-layout routes remain compatibility redirects.

Normal generation preserves every Stable byte. Explicit promotion reads only local Git objects, stages and validates all tagged user outputs, then atomically exchanges the snapshot directory. Promotion runs on Linux or macOS with Python 3 for the operating-system directory swap; normal generation and checking use Node:

node tools/docs/build_static_docs.cjs --promote-stable 1.6.0 --source-ref v1.6.0

The deterministic docs/stable/manifest.json records the release version/ref, exact source commit, original user index, derived page inventory and SHA-256 artifact hashes, without timestamps. --check rejects missing, added or edited Stable files as well as current Next/developer/compatibility drift. Historical pages outside the release's index and developer/source links point to that Git tag. Required release-specific content assets are copied into Stable; shared CSS, logo and navigation assets remain under docs/assets/.

documentation.html is the durable Online Documentation URL and defaults to Stable. Root user bookmarks and doc.html?md=user/... select Stable when its inventory contains the page, otherwise Next; fragments survive redirects. Developer compatibility links continue to current docs/developer/ routes. The channel switcher opens the matching page or explains the missing page and opens the other hub. Next carries noindex,follow; Stable has canonical URLs.

Only the published-release workflow promotes Stable automatically; draft creation does not. See Versioning Policy. Packaged offline Help still corresponds to the exact application release. The product landing, shared presentation assets and developer docs are not versioned. Localization and broader search metadata remain separate work.

Translated mirrors

Translated mirrors belong under docs/user/locales/es/ and docs/user/locales/zh_CN/. Locale identifiers follow the existing localization contract and CMake's PERASTAGE_TRANSLATION_LANGUAGES registry; English (en) is the implicit source and fallback language. There is no separate manual locale registry.

Mirrors use the same filenames and preserve links and page relationships. Translate explanatory prose and preserve exact UI labels according to documentation policy and localization policy. Preserve Console command grammar in English, and standards identifiers such as MVR, GDTF, DMX, XML, and UUID. The supported COMPLETE manual locales are en, es, and zh_CN. English remains the canonical source and fallback. Translated mirrors must maintain exact filename parity with docs/user/*.md, including nonempty UTF-8 content and valid localized heading fragments. F1/Help selects the requested locale from ui_language; page-level English fallback remains available for future development or missing/unreadable files in damaged or incomplete installations.

Runtime and package ownership

cmake/PerastageRuntimeStaging.cmake owns development runtime copies; cmake/PerastageInstall.cmake owns installation and release staging. Both copy only top-level Markdown pages, with no HTML conversion or new build dependency:

<runtime asset root>/
    help/
        en/       # docs/user/*.md, including index.md
        es/       # docs/user/locales/es/*.md, complete mirror
        zh_CN/    # docs/user/locales/zh_CN/*.md, complete mirror

The asset root remains beside the executable on Windows/Linux and inside Perastage.app/Contents/Resources on macOS. All three complete manuals are required release payloads, including in builds with UI localization disabled. CMake tolerates absent localized directories for development fixtures; release guards require every canonical filename in help/en/, help/es/, and help/zh_CN/, including index.md, with staged and installed files byte-identical to their source pages. Locales are never recursively copied into help/en/. Links to developer/reference documents still resolve in the repository/website; these documents are outside the packaged user-manual bundle. The offline viewer opens safe developer/reference links in the repository through the system browser; user-manual links and heading fragments navigate locally. Back restores the previous page, Home returns to index.md, and Online Documentation remains available in both the dialog and Help menu.

Help and Console consumers

F1/Help consumes the canonical packaged help/<locale>/index.md manual. Console consumes only the English marked section from help/en/shortcuts-and-command-bar.md, resolved through the same runtime resource contract. UI language does not select Console syntax or help prose.

In Shortcuts and Command Bar, the invisible HTML comments <!-- PERASTAGE_CONSOLE_HELP_BEGIN --> and <!-- PERASTAGE_CONSOLE_HELP_END --> delimit the canonical Console reference, including transform spaces. Core's user_manual/console_help helper requires exactly one of each marker, in order, and a nonempty section. It uses the bounded MarkdownToPlainText transformation in core/markdown for headings, paragraphs, lists, fenced examples, inline code, bold, links and tables; it does not implement full CommonMark. Missing pages, invalid markers or empty/malformed presentation return only a short English unavailability message and an Online Documentation pointer, with no built-in command catalog. Localized mirrors preserve the markers, but Console always loads English. General keyboard and viewer shortcuts remain outside the marked reference.

Root help.md no longer exists and is neither staged nor installed. There is no independent in-app help prose source: permanent operator-content changes belong in docs/user/*.md, translated mirrors in docs/user/locales/<locale>/*.md, and help/<locale>/*.md is generated/staged package content.

Validation

tests/check_docs_links.py derives filename parity from canonical pages and locales from CMake, checks UTF-8, Console markers and stable command examples, and validates translated links and fragments using the offline anchor rules. MarkdownRenderer verifies fragments against actual rendered headings in every manual. UserManualDialog exercises localized navigation and deliberate page-removal fallback; UserManualStaging verifies the production staging and installation owners with complete, partial and absent locale fixtures. Developer links in mirrors use canonical repository URLs so they resolve both from the nested source directories and from the flat packaged locale folders.
